newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to work with Peru to end hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Canada to work with Peru to end hostage crisis.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Wednesday that Canada would work with Peru to try to secure the release of 200 hostages held by armed guerrillas at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"Canada will cooperate closely with the Peruvian authorities in their efforts to bring this crisis to a resolution, with the safe release of hostages," Chretien's office said in a statement.

Canada's ambassador to Peru, Anthony Vincent, is among the hostages held by the leftist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MTRA) since Tuesday night. The gunmen have threatened to kill them unless the Peruvian government frees jailed guerrillas.

"Canada condemns all acts of international terrorism. There is no justification for such wanton acts of violence," Chretien said. "We will continue to act in close concert with countries that fight against the scourge of terrorism."
